meta.gate: Option C: all decades scored on ESTABLISHED rows only; non-ESTABLISHED rows excluded and named.

weighting_labels.W1: frontier-forward (innovation + science x1.5; structurally favors the US)
weighting_labels.W2: build-and-develop (infrastructure + industrial + social + governmental_economic x1.5; structurally favors China)
weighting_labels.W3: event-type frontier (discovery + invention + founding x1.5; a US-leaning cross-check on a different axis)

caption: Constructed momentum index (OPEN-CAVEATED) - NOT a measured fact. Primary series: baseline equal weighting W0, within-decade share N0, ESTABLISHED rows only. EXCLUDED and not scored: CN-1952-1 (OPEN-UNVERIFIED, 1946-1955); CN-1952-2 (REPORTED, 1946-1955) - understates China in 1946-1955 (the whiskers on that decade show the corrected range if those rows were established). Coloured bands span all four published weightings W0-W3; where a country's band crosses the halfway line, defensible weightings disagree on who leads that decade - those decades (1976-1985, 1986-1995, 1996-2005) are findings, not results. The final 2016-2025 bar is the last full decade; the 2026 window is not yet closed. Re-weight it yourself: the rubric is published and versioned in notes/scoring_rubric_DESIGN.md and scoring/weights.json.

spine_caption: The Century Spine - one block per corpus row at its anchor year, US stacking up from the centreline and China down (1926-2026). RAW COUNTS under the published selection rule (notes/selection_criteria.md) and its density target - a fact ABOUT THE CORPUS, not a momentum score: 270 rows (US 143, China 127), of which 268 ESTABLISHED (solid), 1 OPEN-UNVERIFIED (outlined) and 1 REPORTED (hatched). Colour = category (shared legend below). Amendment-4 trajectory rows sit at their span-start year with a small forward tick. Each block links to its year dossier (dossier.html#y-YYYY).
dossiers_html:
One card per ESTABLISHED ledger row, grouped by decade and year. Deep-linkable: every year heading is an anchor (#y-YYYY) that the Century Spine links into. This mirrors claim_ledger.csv exactly.

1926–1935 24

1926

US-1926-1ESTABLISHEDUS

Robert Goddard launches the world's first liquid-fueled rocket at Auburn, Massachusetts.

science · first-flight/launch · source: official-national
US-1926-2ESTABLISHEDUS

NBC launches as the first permanent national radio broadcasting network in the US.

innovation · founding · source: official-national

1927

US-1927-1ESTABLISHEDUS

Charles Lindbergh completes the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight (New York–Paris) in the Spirit of St. Louis.

science · first-flight/launch · source: official-national
US-1927-2ESTABLISHEDUS

Philo Farnsworth demonstrates the first working all-electronic television image transmission.

innovation · invention · source: encyclopedic | journalistic
US-1927-3ESTABLISHEDUS

The Jazz Singer premieres as the first feature-length film with synchronized recorded dialogue, launching the sound-film era.

innovation · commercial-deployment · source: official-national

1928

CN-1928-1ESTABLISHEDChina

The Northern Expedition ends with nominal national reunification under the Nationalist (KMT) government seated at Nanjing.

governmental_economic · milestone · source: encyclopedic | encyclopedic
CN-1928-2ESTABLISHEDChina

Academia Sinica (中央研究院), China's national academy of sciences, is founded at Nanjing.

science · founding · source: independent-academic
CN-1928-3ESTABLISHEDChina

The Central Bank of China is established in Shanghai as the Nationalist government's central bank.

governmental_economic · founding · source: independent-academic

1929

CN-1929-1ESTABLISHEDChina

Pei Wenzhong discovers the first Peking Man (Homo erectus) skullcap at Zhoukoudian.

science · discovery · source: independent-academic

1930

CN-1930-2ESTABLISHEDChina

China completes the restoration of tariff autonomy as the last major power accedes, ending foreign control over Chinese customs tariff rates. Anchor justification: treaty sequence US 1928 -> most powers by end-1928 -> new tariff effective Feb 1929 -> Japan (last major power) 6 May 1930; anchored to the 1930 completion.

governmental_economic · milestone · source: independent-academic
US-1930-1ESTABLISHEDUS

Clyde Tombaugh discovers Pluto at Lowell Observatory, the first trans-Neptunian object found.

science · discovery · source: encyclopedic | independent-academic

1931

CN-1931-1ESTABLISHEDChina

Liang Shuming establishes the Shandong Rural Reconstruction Institute at Zouping, a landmark rural-reconstruction and mass-education experiment.

social · founding · source: independent-academic
US-1931-1ESTABLISHEDUS

The Empire State Building is completed in New York City, then the tallest building in the world (381 m).

infrastructure · completion · source: encyclopedic | independent-academic
US-1931-2ESTABLISHEDUS

Ernest Lawrence builds the first working cyclotron at Berkeley, enabling particle acceleration.

science · invention · source: official-national

1932

CN-1932-1ESTABLISHEDChina

By ~1932 the Rong family's Shenxin cotton mills were China's largest industrial employer (~31,700 workers across nine mills, roughly a fifth of Chinese-owned spindles); with the Maoxin/Fuxin flour mills the Rong group was the country's largest private industrial enterprise - the 'flour and textile kings'.

industrial · milestone · source: independent-academic|encyclopedic

1933

CN-1933-1ESTABLISHEDChina

China's 'abolish the tael, adopt the yuan' reform standardizes the silver dollar (yuan) as the national monetary unit, replacing the tael.

governmental_economic · milestone · source: independent-academic
US-1933-1ESTABLISHEDUS

The Tennessee Valley Authority is established, a federal authority for regional electrification and river development.

governmental_economic · founding · source: official-national
US-1933-2ESTABLISHEDUS

The Glass–Steagall Banking Act creates federal deposit insurance (FDIC) and separates commercial and investment banking.

governmental_economic · milestone · source: official-national

1935

CN-1935-1ESTABLISHEDChina

The fabi (法币) currency reform abandons the silver standard and unifies a managed national paper currency.

governmental_economic · milestone · source: independent-academic
CN-1935-2ESTABLISHEDChina

The Chinese Communist Party's Red Army completes the Long March, consolidating Mao Zedong's leadership and the CCP's survival.

governmental_economic · milestone · source: encyclopedic | independent-academic
US-1935-1ESTABLISHEDUS

The Social Security Act establishes national old-age pensions and unemployment insurance.

social · milestone · source: official-national
US-1935-2ESTABLISHEDUS

Hoover Dam on the Colorado River is completed, then the world's largest concrete structure and hydroelectric dam.

infrastructure · completion · source: official-national
US-1935-3ESTABLISHEDUS

Wallace Carothers's team at DuPont first synthesizes nylon, the first fully synthetic polymer fiber.

innovation · invention · source: independent-academic
US-1935-4ESTABLISHEDUS

The Douglas DC-3 makes its first flight, becoming the airliner that made passenger air travel commercially viable.

innovation · first-flight/launch · source: official-national
1936–1945 20

1936

CN-1936-1ESTABLISHEDChina

The Canton-Hankow (Yuehan) Railway is completed, linking Guangzhou to Wuhan as a major north-south trunk line.

infrastructure · completion · source: independent-academic

1937

CN-1937-1ESTABLISHEDChina

The Qiantang River Bridge at Hangzhou, chief-engineered by Mao Yisheng, opens as the first modern double-deck road-and-rail bridge designed and built by Chinese engineers.

infrastructure · completion · source: encyclopedic | official-national
US-1937-1ESTABLISHEDUS

The Golden Gate Bridge opens in San Francisco, then the world's longest suspension-bridge main span.

infrastructure · completion · source: official-national

1938

CN-1938-1ESTABLISHEDChina

The National Southwestern Associated University (Xinan Lianda) forms in Kunming, merging Peking, Tsinghua, and Nankai universities to preserve higher education through the war.

science · founding · source: independent-academic
CN-1938-2ESTABLISHEDChina

The Chinese Industrial Cooperatives ('Gung Ho') movement organizes decentralized wartime production across the interior.

industrial · milestone · source: independent-academic
CN-1938-3ESTABLISHEDChina

The Yunnan section of the Burma Road (Kunming to Wanting at the Burmese border, ~960 km), built by an estimated 200,000 Chinese laborers under Nationalist direction, opens to motor traffic in 1938. [Alt anchor: formal completion sometimes dated 1939; both recorded. Narrowed to the Chinese-built Yunnan section per batch-3 ruling.]

infrastructure · completion · source: encyclopedic | journalistic
CN-1938-4ESTABLISHEDChina

The Yichang evacuation (Oct-Dec 1938): Lu Zuofu's Minsheng Shipping Company moves 30,000+ people and ~100,000 tons of supplies - including key industrial equipment - up the Yangtze through the Three Gorges to Sichuan in about 40 days before Yichang's fall, saving much of China's wartime industrial base (the 'Dunkirk of Chinese industry').

industrial · milestone · source: independent-academic|encyclopedic
US-1938-1ESTABLISHEDUS

Chester Carlson produces the first xerographic image, inventing electrophotography (later Xerox copying).

innovation · invention · source: independent-academic

1939

US-1939-1ESTABLISHEDUS

Hewlett-Packard is founded in Palo Alto, an origin point of what became Silicon Valley.

innovation · founding · source: independent-academic

1942

US-1942-1ESTABLISHEDUS

Enrico Fermi's team achieves the first controlled, self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction (Chicago Pile-1).

science · invention · source: official-national
US-1942-2ESTABLISHEDUS

Grand Coulee Dam on the Columbia River is completed, the largest concrete structure and hydroelectric plant in the US.

infrastructure · completion · source: official-national
US-1942-3ESTABLISHEDUS

Over 1942-1945, US wartime industrial mobilization mass-produces war materiel at unprecedented scale (~300,000 aircraft and ~2,700 Liberty ships across the war).

industrial · milestone · source: independent-academic|encyclopedic

1943

CN-1943-1ESTABLISHEDChina

The US and UK relinquish extraterritorial rights in China by treaty, ending a century of the 'unequal treaties'.

governmental_economic · milestone · source: official-national
US-1943-1ESTABLISHEDUS

US pharmaceutical firms achieve deep-tank fermentation mass production of penicillin, enabling the first antibiotic at scale.

science · commercial-deployment · source: official-national

1944

US-1944-1ESTABLISHEDUS

The Bretton Woods conference establishes the IMF and the framework for the World Bank, anchoring the postwar monetary order.

governmental_economic · founding · source: international-body
US-1944-2ESTABLISHEDUS

The GI Bill (Servicemen's Readjustment Act) funds mass higher education and home ownership for returning veterans.

social · milestone · source: official-national

1945

CN-1945-1ESTABLISHEDChina

China becomes a founding member of the United Nations and a permanent member of the Security Council.

governmental_economic · milestone · source: international-body
US-1945-1ESTABLISHEDUS

ENIAC, the first general-purpose electronic digital computer, becomes operational.

innovation · invention · source: independent-academic
US-1945-2ESTABLISHEDUS

The Manhattan Project achieves the first nuclear detonation (Trinity test), demonstrating engineered nuclear fission at scale.

science · invention · source: official-national
US-1945-3ESTABLISHEDUS

Vannevar Bush's report 'Science, the Endless Frontier' sets the blueprint for federal funding of basic research (leading to the NSF).

governmental_economic · milestone · source: official-national
1946–1955 22

1947

US-1947-1ESTABLISHEDUS

Bell Labs invents the point-contact transistor (Bardeen, Brattain, Shockley), foundation of all modern electronics.

science · invention · source: independent-academic
US-1947-2ESTABLISHEDUS

Chuck Yeager pilots the Bell X-1 to the first crewed supersonic flight, breaking the sound barrier.

science · first-flight/launch · source: official-national
US-1947-3ESTABLISHEDUS

Levittown, New York begins mass-produced suburban housing, a template for postwar American suburbanization.

social · commercial-deployment · source: encyclopedic | encyclopedic

1948

US-1948-1ESTABLISHEDUS

The Marshall Plan (European Recovery Program) begins large-scale US-funded reconstruction of Western Europe.

governmental_economic · milestone · source: official-national
US-1948-2ESTABLISHEDUS

Claude Shannon publishes 'A Mathematical Theory of Communication', founding information theory.

science · invention · source: independent-academic

1949

CN-1949-1ESTABLISHEDChina

The People's Republic of China is founded, ending decades of civil war and fragmentation on the mainland.

governmental_economic · founding · source: independent-academic
US-1949-1ESTABLISHEDUS

The US leads the founding of NATO, the postwar transatlantic security institution.

governmental_economic · founding · source: international-body

1950

CN-1950-1ESTABLISHEDChina

The Marriage Law of 1950 bans arranged and child marriage and establishes new legal rights for women.

social · milestone · source: independent-academic
CN-1950-2ESTABLISHEDChina

Nationwide Land Reform (1950-1953) redistributes land from landlords to peasants under the 1950 Agrarian Reform Law.

social · milestone · source: encyclopedic | independent-academic
CN-1950-3ESTABLISHEDChina

The new government halts hyperinflation and stabilizes the renminbi, restoring monetary order.

governmental_economic · milestone · source: independent-academic

1951

US-1951-1ESTABLISHEDUS

UNIVAC I is delivered as the first commercially produced electronic computer in the US.

innovation · commercial-deployment · source: encyclopedic | official-national

1952

CN-1952-3ESTABLISHEDChina

The Patriotic Health Campaign mobilizes mass sanitation and disease-control drives nationwide.

social · milestone · source: independent-academic
US-1952-1ESTABLISHEDUS

The US detonates 'Ivy Mike', the first full-scale thermonuclear (hydrogen) device.

science · invention · source: official-national

1953

CN-1953-1ESTABLISHEDChina

The First Five-Year Plan (1953-1957) begins Soviet-aided heavy industrialization built around 156 key projects.

industrial · milestone · source: independent-academic
CN-1953-2ESTABLISHEDChina

China conducts its first modern national census, counting roughly 583 million people. [Conflicting figures recorded: official count 582.6M (1953) vs the prior ~450M League of Nations 1933 estimate; G. Cressey questioned the count as inflated, though later scholarship assessed ~100% coverage.]

governmental_economic · milestone · source: independent-academic
US-1953-1ESTABLISHEDUS

The NTSC color television standard is adopted, launching compatible color broadcasting in the US.

innovation · commercial-deployment · source: official-national

1954

CN-1954-1ESTABLISHEDChina

The first Constitution of the PRC is adopted and the first National People's Congress convenes.

governmental_economic · milestone · source: independent-academic
US-1954-1ESTABLISHEDUS

USS Nautilus is commissioned as the world's first nuclear-powered submarine.

innovation · commercial-deployment · source: official-national
US-1954-2ESTABLISHEDUS

Bell Labs demonstrates the first practical silicon solar cell.

science · invention · source: independent-academic

1955

CN-1955-1ESTABLISHEDChina

Qian Xuesen returns from the US to China, seeding the country's missile and later space programs.

science · milestone · source: encyclopedic | journalistic
US-1955-1ESTABLISHEDUS

Jonas Salk's inactivated polio vaccine is licensed after mass field trials, curbing a feared epidemic disease.

science · commercial-deployment · source: encyclopedic | independent-academic
US-1955-2ESTABLISHEDUS

Ray Kroc launches the McDonald's franchise system, a template for standardized mass-service industry.

innovation · founding · source: independent-academic | journalistic
1956–1965 28

1956

CN-1956-1ESTABLISHEDChina

The First Automobile Works produces the Jiefang CA-10 truck, the first motor vehicle manufactured in China.

innovation · commercial-deployment · source: encyclopedic | journalistic
CN-1956-2ESTABLISHEDChina

The 'socialist transformation' of industry and commerce is completed, converting private enterprise to public/joint ownership.

governmental_economic · milestone · source: independent-academic
CN-1956-3ESTABLISHEDChina

China's State Council promulgates the first Scheme for Simplifying Chinese Characters (515 simplified characters plus 54 radicals), a mass-literacy language reform.

social · milestone · source: independent-academic
US-1956-1ESTABLISHEDUS

The Federal-Aid Highway Act launches the Interstate Highway System, the largest US public-works program.

infrastructure · milestone · source: official-national
US-1956-2ESTABLISHEDUS

IBM ships the RAMAC 305, the first computer with a moving-head hard disk drive.

innovation · commercial-deployment · source: encyclopedic | journalistic

1957

CN-1957-1ESTABLISHEDChina

The Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge opens, the first bridge to span the Yangtze, carrying rail and road.

infrastructure · completion · source: independent-academic
US-1957-1ESTABLISHEDUS

The Shippingport Atomic Power Station begins operation as the first full-scale commercial nuclear power plant in the United States.

infrastructure · completion · source: official-national

1958

CN-1958-1ESTABLISHEDChina

Hanyu Pinyin romanization is adopted, complementing simplified characters in a national literacy drive.

social · milestone · source: independent-academic
US-1958-1ESTABLISHEDUS

NASA is established as the US civilian space agency.

governmental_economic · founding · source: official-national
US-1958-2ESTABLISHEDUS

Explorer 1, the first US satellite, reaches orbit and discovers the Van Allen radiation belts.

science · first-flight/launch · source: official-national
US-1958-3ESTABLISHEDUS

Jack Kilby at Texas Instruments demonstrates the first integrated circuit.

innovation · invention · source: independent-academic
US-1958-4ESTABLISHEDUS

The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (ARPA/DARPA) is established, seeding foundational US technologies (packet networking, GPS, stealth, autonomy).

governmental_economic · founding · source: official-national
US-1958-5ESTABLISHEDUS

The Boeing 707 enters commercial service with Pan Am, inaugurating the jet age of mass commercial air travel. [Commercial service began 26 Oct 1958 (Pan Am); prototype first flight 20 Dec 1957 recorded as alternative anchor.]

innovation · commercial-deployment · source: encyclopedic | journalistic

1959

CN-1959-1ESTABLISHEDChina

The Daqing oilfield is discovered, launching China's path to petroleum self-sufficiency. [Era context: within the Great Leap Forward (1958-1962) - context, not adjudication; oil self-sufficiency (~1963) a later consequence.]

industrial · discovery · source: independent-academic
CN-1959-2ESTABLISHEDChina

The Great Hall of the People and the 'Ten Great Buildings' are completed for the PRC's tenth anniversary. [Era context: one of the Great Leap Forward's 'Ten Great Buildings', realised in ~10 months by ~8,000 workers.]

infrastructure · completion · source: encyclopedic | encyclopedic
